#### **Aim :**
To generate a vector of 20 elements in R and perform operations such as checking its class and type, converting it into a complex vector, extracting elements, and creating matrices using row-wise and column-wise binding.

#### **Theory :**
In R, a **vector** is a one-dimensional data structure that stores
elements of the same data type. The `seq()` function is used to generate
a sequence of numbers with a specified starting value, increment, and
length. The `class()` and `typeof()` functions are used to determine the
class and underlying data type of a vector.

A numeric vector can be converted into a **complex vector** using the
`as.complex()` function. Individual elements of a vector can be accessed
using their index position. The `rbind()` function is used to combine
data **row-wise**, while `cbind()` is used to combine data **column-wise**.
The functions `is.vector()` and `is.matrix()` are used to test whether
an object is a vector or a matrix.

#### **Problem :**
Generate a vector of 20 elements starting with 2.5 by a jump of 0.3 and perform the following tasks :
```{r}
# Generating the vector
x <- seq(2.5, by = 0.3, length.out = 20)

cat("The generated vector is :",x)
```
**I.** Check the class and types of this vector.
```{r}
cat("The class of the vector is :",class(x))
cat("The type of the vector is :",typeof(x))
```
**II.** Convert this to complex vector and save with name z.
```{r}
# Converting to complex vector
z <- as.complex(x)
cat("The converted vecor is :",z)
```
**III.** Extract all the elements which is at the eleven places.
```{r}
# Extracting the 11th element of the vector
cat("The element which is at eleventh places is :",x[11])
```
**IV.** Extract the first five elements. Thereafter bind them row wise and column wise; and store under the name row_mat.Perform the testing for matrix and vector.
```{r}
# Extracting the first 5 elements
first5 <- x[1:5]
cat("The first five elements of the vector is :",first5)
# Binding them row-wise
row_mat <- rbind(first5)
cat("Matrix after binding row-wise :",row_mat)
# checking its type
cat("The row_mat is a vector :",is.vector(row_mat))
cat("The row_mat is a matrix :",is.matrix(row_mat))
# Binding them column-wise
col_mat <- cbind(first5)
cat("Matrix after binding column-wise :",col_mat)
# checking its type
cat("The col_mat is a vector :",is.vector(col_mat))
cat("The col_mat is a matrix :",is.matrix(col_mat))
# checking the type of original vector
cat("x is a vector :",is.vector(x))
cat("x is a matrix :",is.matrix(x))
```

#### **Result :**
The vector of 20 elements was successfully created in R using `seq()`. Its class and type were identified, and it was successfully converted into a complex vector. The required elements were extracted, and row-wise and column-wise matrices were created using `rbind()` and `cbind()`. The vector and matrix objects were also successfully tested using `is.vector()` and `is.matrix()`.
